data.statement:
My research interests center on software engineering — software quality, vulnerability detection, and the empirical study of how real systems are built and maintained. My M.Sc. thesis works directly in this space, studying software vulnerability: what makes a method risky, and whether a model can tell us before it breaks.

I am equally drawn to natural language processing, deep learning, and generative models. My B.Sc. thesis came from that side: PairSiamNet, a transformer-enhanced Siamese network that learns an embedding space where distance reflects semantic relatedness.

Across both, what draws me is application — work that ends in something useful, not just a better number.

interests.title: Software Quality & Maintenance
interests.text: What makes software reliable, readable, and maintainable over its lifetime.

interests.title: Software Vulnerability & Security
interests.text: Finding weaknesses in code before they become failures in production.

interests.title: Empirical Software Engineering
interests.text: Studying how software is actually built, using evidence drawn from real projects.

interests.title: AI for Software Engineering
interests.text: What changes in software when machines take on more of the writing and reviewing.

interests.title: Natural Language Processing
interests.text: Teaching machines to represent meaning in language, and in code.

interests.title: Deep Learning & Generative Models
interests.text: How modern architectures learn, generate, and where their limits lie.
